correctness.rationale: The exterior-product/midpoint diameter lemma has a fully derived inequality and equality case. For doubly stochastic matrices, pairwise Frobenius diameters force disjoint permutations; one overlapping entry imposes the exact n>=5 second-level upper bound. A cyclic construction attains it at every n>=5. The n=4 exceptional second level is certified by explicit exhaustive integer Gram determinants over all 1,771 anchor-normalized quadruples. The independent direct-matrix Gram path confirms selected cases; all hypotheses and the vertex-only second-level restriction are stated.

value.rationale: The natural problem of selecting four assignments with maximal 3-dimensional Euclidean spread has a sharp first stability gap and complete single-overlap equality configurations for every order >=5. This supplies an exact metric robustness criterion for Latin-rectangle-like sets of permutations and a small-order packing obstruction, neither implied by previously checked Chebyshev radii or face counts. A separate finite count is supplementary, not the sole justification for value.
